Case A

A1: The search of the past seven days showed only the earlier requests from the stable region and fingerprint. The key was published, then the burst came 19 minutes later. The search window covers the period before publication, so there was no earlier misuse in that window. But did the search cover the time after publication and before the 19 minutes? Yes, the past seven days would include it, and it returned only the earlier requests, which suggests nothing else before the burst. Still, "past seven days" is relative to the search time, and the publication date is unknown. The key may have been used before the search window, and the search only returned the earlier requests, which were the legitimate ones. Within the window, the burst appears to be the first non-baseline use. Whether the key was misused earlier outside the window or through unlogged means cannot be determined, so I answer Cannot tell.

A2: The compromise check did not flag the account. Whether evidence was available to it is not clear. The shared payout destination was on record from before, and the burst had occurred 11 minutes earlier. The check scored 30 minutes after publication, so the burst data (19 minutes) and the payout destination record were plausibly available. But we don't know what the check uses as inputs, so Cannot tell.

A3: A shared payout destination does not by itself show one owner. Answer: No, not by itself.

A4: The absence of reports after 30 days does not indicate legitimacy, given the circumstances, though it is weak evidence at most. The options are "Yes, weakly", "No", and "Cannot tell". Absence of a recorded report can reflect no detection or no reporting. I choose No, since no report or finding is not evidence of legitimacy here.

A5: Yes, it warrants investigation.

Case B

B1: D has 0 chargebacks vs 2 for the others, on 100 transactions each. The recorded rate is lower (0% vs 2%). Yes.

B2: A combined measure of 5% does not show that no single account is above 5%, because the measure includes alerts and is aggregated. Per-account figures could differ. Answer: No.

B3: The search found no accounts beyond A and the closed account, but it only covers the data searched, and the person might use other names. Also the person appears on the closed account, which is not an active merchant account. Cannot tell whether other accounts exist under other identities. Answer: No, the search does not show that. The question is "Does the search show that the controlling person has no other merchant accounts?" Answer: No.

B4: Two notes by different analysts on different days may not be independent, as they could rely on the same evidence. Cannot tell.

B5: No. A blocked payment with no chargeback is not shown to be non-fraud, because it was blocked as suspected fraud and so no chargeback would arise.

B6: Yes, shared templates and descriptor patterns justify investigating together.

RESULT CN-004 | A1: Cannot tell | A2: Cannot tell | A3: No, not by itself | A4: No | A5: Yes | B1: Yes | B2: No | B3: No | B4: Cannot tell | B5: No | B6: Yes
